subject: Hosted API capacity & pricing — quick qual + next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-18T14:10:00Z
Subject: Hosted API capacity & pricing — quick qual + next steps

Hi Emma — great to meet today, thanks for walking us through Veridian's ingestion and inference patterns. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can size a hosted pricing estimate that reflects your peaks. Please confirm the items below by EOD so we can push an initial quote by tomorrow afternoon.

Call recap / ask-back:
- Primary workload: realtime QA and summarization for clinician notes (model calls on every saved note).
- Expected steady-state monthly tokens: you mentioned ~120M–160M / month. Please confirm a tighter range if possible.
- Peak TPS: you said ~220 TPS sustained, with short daily bursts up to ~800 TPS for ~10 minutes (traffic tied to shift handoffs). Please confirm burst duration and frequency.
- Budget target: you called out unit economics target of ~$500 / 1M tokens as aspirational — is that the target for hosted (no reserved capacity) or for a committed contract?
- Timeline: pilot in June (1–2 months), GA in Q3 bearing capacity readiness.

What we'll produce if you confirm:
- Hosted API cost bands (no-commit, 3mo commit, 6–12mo commit) with an example cost calc at 150M tokens.
- Peak TPS sizing guidance and whether we recommend prefix/KV caching or a small reserved burst pool to flatten costs.
- A simple usage template (attached) to help you map daily patterns for more accurate sizing.

Attachments: Veridian_usage_template.csv (please fill and return)

Next steps:
- You confirm the two numbers above (monthly token range, burst / peak TPS) + preferred $/1M target.
- We provide a hosted quote and propose a 30-min follow-up Wed to walk numbers.

Thanks — Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Tessa — solid recap. Confirming the numbers you called out with a little more color: 
- Steady-state monthly tokens: we expect 120M in month 1 ramping to ~160M by month 6 as automation adoption grows. Conservatively plan for 140M if that helps quotes.
- Peak TPS: 220 TPS sustained for roughly 2–3 hours during West Coast day overlap; + short bursts to 750–800 TPS for about 8–12 minutes once per day (shift change). Bursts are predictable (07:00–07:15 UTC).
- Budget target: the $500 / 1M tokens figure is our internal target but applies to a hosted + committed plan. For no-commit hosted we'd expect higher.

A few asks from our side: 
- Can you show an example month cost at 140M tokens for both no-commit and a 6-month commitment?
- Any guidance if we maintain two model sizes (base vs. opt-quantized) and call routing adds cost?

Attaching our architecture slide for reference. Happy to take the Wed slot if you have availability 14:00–16:00 PT.

--
Emma Li
Head of Product 
Veridian Health
Attachments: Veridian_prod_arch.pdf
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-04-19T09:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity & pricing — quick qual + next steps

Emma — thanks for the confirmation and the architecture doc; helpful. Below is an initial hosted pricing sketch (ballpark) based on the 140M token example you requested and the burst/peak profile. These are estimates; final quote will include committed discounts and SLA specifics.

Example cost for 140M tokens / month (hosted API):
- No-commit (on-demand hosted): unit price $720 / 1M tokens -> approx $100,800 / month
- 3-month commit (volume band): unit price $620 / 1M tokens -> approx $86,800 / month
- 6-month commit (preferred tier): unit price $470 / 1M tokens -> approx $65,800 / month

Notes on unit economics & peak TPS: 
- Short intense bursts (750–800 TPS) increase provisioning needs; for hosted we typically handle bursts with autoscaling + short-lived burst capacity. That adds ~10–18% to effective cost in the no-commit case; with a committed plan we can size a small reserved burst pool to reduce marginal burst cost.
- If you route some traffic to a quantized model variant (lower-cost tokens but higher latency risk), we can reflect a hybrid unit price. Example: mixed routing (75% base, 25% quantized) yields an effective unit price ~10–12% lower than base.

Example calc (6-month commit): 140M tokens * $470/1M = $65,800 / month (excl. any overage/ingress).

Attachments: preliminary hosted quote (I will produce a PDF with line-items and send after we agree on commitment window).

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm whether the 6-month commit is viable or if you prefer 3-months / on-demand.
2) If 6-months, we can present a structured quote with volume tiers, a modest first-year discount option, and an SLA.
3) Schedule the Wed 14:00–14:30 PT call to walk the numbers (I have that slot tentatively).

Sharing HubSpot link to deal for internal tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345

Cheers — Tessa
